cells.tense: You are at the bench now, and the clearing has already happened.
cells.ask: Pick the one piece of the work that would show a flaw if you looked closely, and look at it closely today — once, unhurried, no fixing yet.
cells.core:
The clearing came through and what it took down needed to go. You're still at the bench, and the thing in your hands is getting truer with each pass.

What's working is that you can sit with one piece long enough for the flaws to show themselves, and you don't flinch when they do. You're not rushing to the end of it and not defending the part you already made. The refining is steady — it adds up rather than burning anything down. Stay where the work can still teach you something. That's the whole of it: keep the pass slow and let the piece tell you what it needs.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a collapse that has not happened and may never come.
cells.ask: Show one unfinished piece to one person today, before it's ready — say what it is, not what it will be.
cells.core:
You're building ahead of the building. Somewhere in front of you there's a version where everything holds and the structure is finally right, and you're already there in your head — so every pass becomes a test of whether it will hold. The work has stopped being work and become a verdict you're waiting on.

That's what's bending it. The clearing you're braced for isn't coming from outside; you're rehearsing it with every detail you check twice. What feeds this instead is letting something be seen before it's finished, and letting that be enough. It doesn't have to be good. It has to be shown, once, and left alone after that.

cells.tense: The clearing already happened and you are still standing at the old door.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person or just the room, the one thing you make or do — name it plainly, no explaining why it matters.
cells.core:
The structure came down and you're still living where it was. Not because you miss it, but because nothing has replaced it — no work in your hands, nothing that asks you to come back tomorrow. The clearing did its work. What's absent is the next thing to build.

When this is going well, you pick a thing, say plainly what it is, and the saying carries you back to what you do. That's the way back — your own voice before your hands. It doesn't need to be impressive. It needs to be said where someone could hear it, including you.

cells.tense: You are already at the bench, but you talk as if the work were happening to you.
cells.ask: Take one thing you did today and say, just to yourself, "I did that" — no story about why it was easy or obvious.
cells.core:
You're already deep in it. The hours at the bench, the piece getting truer, the returning to it when it would be easier not to — all of that is running. But when you describe it, it comes out as if the work were something you happened to be near, or something that needed doing, or a habit you fell into.

The decision is there and the saying-so isn't. That's the only gap. Nobody else is making the call about how the piece goes; you are, each time you sit down. Saying it once, without dressing it up, brings the two back into the same room. It's a small move and it's the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: The work is yours. You've been describing it like a habit.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the reader is at a real threshold of mastery through sustained craft — the record doesn't establish they have a practice at all, only that the capacity is seated where false structures clear. The reader could reasonably say this is about a job ending, a relationship ending, or a decision already made, not a craft. The ask survives a wrong read: each is one visible act today that costs nothing, and none depends on my being right about what the structure was. The sentence that serves me is any line implying the collapse was earned or that the mastery is already in hand — both flatter the reading rather than the person.
